body.x: The ‘Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026)’ hosted the ‘FIX 2026 Global Media Awards’ on the 23rd at the FIX TV Zone inside EXCO West Wing in Daegu.

Organized by FIX 2026 and co-hosted by official media partner AVING News, the ‘BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards’ brought together ten global media outlets invited from three regions—Europe, the Americas, and Asia—to introduce the core technologies and flagship products of each publication’s selected TOP 3 enterprises, illuminating their competitive strengths across international markets.

Held under the slogan ‘Startup City Daegu’, the ceremony was emceed by AVING News reporter Thomas Frederiksen and opened with congratulatory remarks by Mi-jung Kim, Team Leader of the Future Mobility Division at Daegu Metropolitan City. Announcements and trophy presentations followed for the 30 recognized companies, each representing a media partner’s TOP 3 picks.

body.cap: Opening with welcoming remarks from Mi-jung Kim, Team Leader of the Future Mobility Division at Daegu Metropolitan City, under the banner of ‘Startup City Daegu’ | Photo by AVING News
TOP 3 enterprises selected by Editor-in-Chief Leo Thevenet of Le Café du Geek: BEYLESS, Brain-Life Link, and TESOLLO | Photo by AVING News

body.x: France’s Le Café du Geek: Capturing Practical Usability Bridging Daily Life and Industry

Editor-in-Chief Leo Thevenet of Le Café du Geek has covered the event in Daegu since DIFA 2023—the precursor to FIX—and has followed it with FIX 2024, 2025, and this year’s edition. Le Café du Geek selected BEYLESS, Brain-Life Link, and TESOLLO. BEYLESS reinforces foundational future mobility with in-vehicle embedded software spanning SDVs, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), AUTOSAR-compliant stacks, and Over-the-Air (OTA) updates. Brain-Life Link integrates biosignals, such as electroencephalograms (EEG), with AI in its wearable ‘Focus+’, designed to assess concentration and relaxation states as a direct-to-consumer technology rather than as a medical device. TESOLLO targets precision manipulation for humanoid and industrial automation systems with its articulated 20-DoF robotic hand, ‘DG-5F’. Thevenet highlighted TESOLLO’s advanced hardware maturity, remarking on the system's remarkable mechanical engineering.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Editor-in-Chief Juan Castromil of Clipset: TOFF MOBILITY, WAVUS, and PYUNGHWA HOLDINGS | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Spain’s Clipset: Expanding Future Mobility Through Electric Aviation, Drone Control, and Manufacturing Innovation

Before presenting his selections, Editor-in-Chief Juan Castromil of Clipset commended the advancements in mobility and control technologies, noting that the exhibition offered a direct preview of future systems. TOFF MOBILITY presented comprehensive integrated operations through services such as ‘EV Air Care’, spanning electric aircraft deployment, fleet maintenance, and flight operations data management. WAVUS demonstrated technology that enables the safe operation and unified management of uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) through drone detection and autonomous control architectures. PYUNGHWA HOLDINGS detailed its technical roadmap for translating its automotive vibration-damping, industrial hose, and elastomer material engineering into impact-absorption components for humanoid and quadruped robots. Castromil noted that TOFF MOBILITY’s electric aircraft framework held the strongest appeal.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Editor-in-Chief Eliane Fiolet of Ubergizmo: Doosan Robotics, DOGU Robotics, and Rezbin Waste Technology | Photo by AVING News

body.x: U.S. Ubergizmo: Spotlighting Practical Robotics and Circular Economy Solutions Delivering Immediate Field Efficiency

Visiting Daegu for the second consecutive year following FIX 2025, Editor-in-Chief Eliane Fiolet of Ubergizmo expressed strong appreciation for South Korea’s deep-tech advancements and AI robotics ecosystem. Doosan Robotics was recognized for its field-ready deployment capabilities, highlighted by collaborative robots that share workspaces with humans, along with its software platform ‘Dart-Suite’ and intuitive ‘Scan & Go’ functionality. DOGU Robotics presented facility security solutions that combine AI-autonomous patrol robots with centralized remote management, showcasing a wheeled-legged quadruped robot during this year’s expo. Participating within the ASEAN-Korea Startup Week pavilion, Philippine startup Rezbin Waste Technology was selected for lowering the barrier to waste segregation by logging plastic recycling participation via a mobile application and rewarding users with redeemable points.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by CEO Yoshioka Tomomi of Otaku Soken: MIRAEROBOT, HD Hyundai Robotics, and U&S Networks | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Japan’s Otaku Soken: Focusing on Solutions for Real-World Problems in Robotics Education, Manufacturing Automation, and Centralized Monitoring

Participating as an official global media partner for the first time this year, CEO Yoshioka Tomomi of Otaku Soken noted deep interest in creative hardware execution and practical AI utility. MIRAEROBOT supplies educational robots, coding hardware kits, and AI manipulators, establishing hands-on environments for students and developers to learn robotic motion principles and kinematics firsthand. The enterprise is actively exploring market entry into Japan and Vietnam. HD Hyundai Robotics showcased industrial arms, collaborative robots, Flat Panel Display (FPD) transfer robots, and motion controllers, accelerating factory automation and expansion into Physical AI. U&S Networks introduced an AI-driven centralized command-and-control platform that monitors and operates robots and drones from disparate manufacturers through a single pane of glass, enabling intuitive text- and voice-based facility management across mixed-fleet environments such as hospitals and manufacturing plants.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Research Editor Sherri Wang of DIGITIMES: LVIS Korea, OPTOELEC, and KAR Co., Ltd. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Taiwan’s DIGITIMES: Evaluating Integrated AI, Photonics, and Mobility Technologies with Investment Value and Global Scalability

Returning to Daegu following FIX 2025, Research Editor Sherri Wang of DIGITIMES assessed South Korea’s supply chain competitiveness across Physical AI and robotics. LVIS Korea was recognized for its AI-driven neuro-mapping software ‘NeuroMatch®’, supporting medical professionals in analyzing EEG readings and diagnosing neurological disorders. OPTOELEC targets intelligent automotive headlamp optics and next-generation photonics through Wafer-Level Optics (WLO) that applies semiconductor fabrication processes to optical component manufacturing. KAR Co., Ltd. demonstrated comprehensive mobility engineering expertise—spanning conceptual design, system integration, and full-vehicle validation—alongside its autonomous driving research go-kart platform.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Editor-in-Chief Stephanie Chen of ChinaByte: YHDATABASE, ORGO, and NRT Sensors | Photo by AVING News

body.x: China’s ChinaByte: High Marks for Foundational Software and Core Componentry in the Embodied AI Era

Editor-in-Chief Stephanie Chen of ChinaByte selected three companies after evaluating technological depth, international market potential, industrial design, commercialization readiness, mass-production capabilities, cost competitiveness, and supply chain value. YHDATABASE earned recognition for its data analytics and security capabilities via ‘y-SmartData’, an AI- and big data-driven fraud detection system (FDS). ORGO showcased its ‘ORGO LIFT’ electric lifting actuator engineered to execute vertical lifting motions for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). NRT Sensors presented precision position-sensing solutions, including inductive rotary encoders built to withstand harsh external electromagnetic and environmental interference.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Deputy Editor Dimpal Bajwa of ET Manufacturing: BRATO, D,RIVE, and AeiROBOT | Photo by AVING News

body.x: India’s ET Manufacturing: Highlighting Manufacturing Competitiveness via Precision Reducers, Vehicle Telematics, and Humanoids

Deputy Editor Dimpal Bajwa of ET Manufacturing reviewed South Korea’s technology landscape from the vantage point of India’s expansive manufacturing economy, commending the vibrant ambition across exhibiting startups. BRATO supports high-precision motion control across robotics and automated production machinery with its ‘BP Series’ low-backlash precision planetary gearboxes, designed for direct servo motor coupling. D,RIVE operates as a specialized mobility data intelligence platform, harvesting high-fidelity diagnostics directly from vehicle electronic control units (ECUs) to deliver real-time fleet telematics and driver behavior analytics. AeiROBOT presented automation possibilities for manufacturing, shipbuilding, and construction environments through its ‘ALICE’ bipedal humanoid series, proprietary robotic actuators, and autonomous AI operating systems.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Deputy Editor-in-Chief Võ Hoàng Long of VietnamPlus: Farmity, JINMYUNG I&C, and iM Robotics | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Vietnam’s VietnamPlus: Prioritizing Local Applicability Across Spatial AI, Smart Surveillance, and Autonomous Transport

Covering the exhibition for the second time since FIX 2024, Deputy Editor-in-Chief Võ Hoàng Long of VietnamPlus focused on identifying adaptable solutions and strategic partnership opportunities relevant to Vietnam’s rapidly evolving industrial sectors. Farmity was selected first for its Spatial AI solution, which integrates millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar with computer vision to recognize human postures and environmental hazards. JINMYUNG I&C supports safety across public and industrial facilities through AI-enabled CCTV surveillance and integrated public address/acoustic technologies. iM Robotics addresses material handling bottlenecks with indoor and outdoor autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) tailored to automate logistics and plant transport.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Editor-in-Chief Mubashar Aftab of Pokde.net: STM Corporation, GEOBOT, and Intellectus Corp. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Malaysia’s Pokde.net: Choosing Components, Infrastructure, and Middleware with High Engineering Polish and Field Interoperability

Visiting Daegu for the first time at FIX 2026, Editor-in-Chief Mubashar Aftab of Pokde.net shared that the innovative momentum and distinctive product lineups of South Korean technology firms energized him. Founded in 1972, STM Corporation has leveraged over five decades of automotive precision engineering to showcase high-durability wheel-bearing seals and magnetic encoders. GEOBOT develops Physical AI robotics and digital twin platforms for diagnostics of ground and subsurface infrastructure, building on technology transfers from the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM). Intellectus Corp. introduced its Data Distribution Service (DDS)-based real-time middleware ‘int2ConneX’, engineered to network and synchronize data across heterogeneous industrial machinery.

body.cap: TOP 3 enterprises selected by Davis Kim, Director of AVING USA: MOBILTECH, AIRC Inc., and YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AVING USA: Rewarding Counter-Intuitive Innovations Overcoming Legacy Industrial Plateaus

Davis Kim, Director of AVING USA, defined his selection criteria around companies that either overcame conventional industry plateaus through technical breakthroughs or creatively deployed advanced tech into unexpected commercial verticals. MOBILTECH delivers spatial intelligence and digital twin infrastructure—comprising sensor suites, calibration suites, and its ‘Replica City’ platform—forming a standardized validation foundation for autonomous driving and robotics developers. AIRC Inc. re-engineered retail store operations with ‘PnGO’, an automated AI unmanned robotic convenience store where goods storage, retrieval, and dispensing are handled entirely by robotics; the company designed the compact 33-square-meter footprint to stock and dispense over 1,500 distinct SKUs. YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS demonstrated how Physical AI integrates into commercial lifestyle spaces by expanding collaborative robotics into specialized service domains, including automated ice cream dispensing and non-invasive cellulite-management systems.

body.cap: Trophies of ‘FIX 2026 GLOBAL MEDIA AWARDS’ | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In the Era of Physical AI, Foundational Enablers Prove as Vital as Finished Platforms

The 30 enterprises selected by the ten global media outlets span a diverse range of industries, including robotics, autonomous mobility, embedded software, high-precision sensors, healthcare ICT, and environmental platforms. Notably, the international press covered not only finished systems such as humanoid robots and autonomous shuttles but also foundational enablers: spatial data architectures, precision reducers, inductive encoders, real-time data distribution middleware, and advanced polymers. Across all evaluations, the media partners placed consistent emphasis on verified on-site field viability, operational efficiency, and supply chain readiness rather than purely theoretical benchmarks.

The award-winning enterprises will receive targeted global press coverage through the participating international media partners, accelerating their international visibility and opening expanded collaborative channels with overseas markets.

body.x: Participating media partners for the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards included: Le Café du Geek, Clipset, Ubergizmo, AVING USA, Otaku Soken, DIGITIMES, VietnamPlus, ChinaByte, ET Manufacturing, and Pokde.net.

Throughout FIX 2026, the international press delegation directly engaged in the ‘FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day’ and on-site assessments for the ‘BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards’, reporting on the technological advancements of the enterprises driving South Korea’s future industry forward.
